issues.legal_issue: A minor’s purported relinquishment of an inherited share does not constitute a transfer by a guardian that must be set aside within the limitation period applicable to a ward’s suit against a guardian’s transfer.
material_facts: The claimant had inherited a share in the property before he was adopted, and was a minor when the later revenue mutations were made.

The adoptive father initiated the mutations, but the records reflected the claimant’s own purported relinquishment; they did not record a release made by the adoptive father as the claimant’s guardian.
The claimant sought a declaration of his ownership share.
issues.conclusion: The mutations did not amount to a transfer by the claimant’s guardian, so the limitation rule for a ward seeking to set aside a guardian’s transfer did not bar the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Article 44 of the Limitation Act applies to a suit by a ward to set aside a transfer of property made by a guardian. A minor’s purported release of his own share is legally ineffectual; without a release or transfer by the guardian on the minor’s behalf, Article 44 does not apply. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: declaratory_title_suit and claimant_was_minor_at_mutation and minor_purported_to_relinquish_share and guardian_made_no_release

predicates.declaratory_title_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking a declaration of title to property.
predicates.claimant_was_minor_at_mutation: The claimant was a minor when the disputed property-record entries were made.
predicates.minor_purported_to_relinquish_share: The minor made a statement purporting to relinquish an inherited share.
predicates.guardian_made_no_release: The guardian made no release or transfer of the minor’s share on the minor’s behalf.

issues.definition: When a minor seeks a declaration of title, was recorded as relinquishing an inherited share, and the guardian made no release on the minor’s behalf, the claim is not barred for failure to set aside a guardian’s transfer.

issues.legal_issue: A limitation objection first raised on appeal cannot be entertained when it was not raised in the courts below and the parties had expressly given up any further point in dispute.
material_facts: The respondent argued in the Supreme Court that the declaratory suit was barred by the limitation rule for declaratory relief.
That limitation objection had not been raised in the courts below.
When issues were framed at trial, counsel for both parties recorded that there was no other point in dispute and gave up any point mentioned in the pleadings.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to allow the limitation objection to be raised at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the objection as too late because it had not been raised in the courts below and the parties had expressly given up any further point in dispute when issues were framed. Article 120 of the Limitation Act was invoked by the respondent, but no earlier cases are cited.

predicates.declaratory_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking declaratory relief.
predicates.limitation_objection_not_raised_below: The party did not raise the limitation objection in the courts below.
predicates.further_issue_expressly_given_up: At issue framing, the parties expressly stated that there was no other point in dispute and gave up any further point mentioned in the pleadings.

issues.definition: In a declaratory suit, a limitation objection not raised below is not entertained on appeal when the parties had expressly given up further issues.

issues.legal_issue: A later adoption does not extinguish an inherited share in property that vested before the adoption.
material_facts: The claimant was born during the common ancestor’s lifetime but was adopted by another family member only after the common ancestor died.
Following the common ancestor’s death, the claimant was recorded with another descendant as jointly entitled to a share of the property.
The claimant’s later adoption gave him a further share through his adoptive father, while later revenue entries purported to remove him from his birth father’s inheritance.
The Court restored the trial court’s declaration that the claimant owned three-fourths of the property.
issues.conclusion: The claimant retained his inherited share and was entitled to the further share derived through adoption, for a total three-fourths share.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the claimant’s title to the share inherited before his adoption as well as the share obtained through adoption. It cited no specific provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.property_title_claim_involves_later_adop: The claimant’s title claim concerns inherited property and a later adoption into another family branch.
predicates.inherited_share_vested_before_adoption: The claimant’s inherited share vested before the adoption took place.

issues.definition: When a property title claim involves a later adoption and an inherited share that vested before it, the later adoption does not extinguish that share.
